newsitem.title: USA: US EPA takes regulatory step on clean car program.
newsitem.headline: US EPA takes regulatory step on clean car program.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency on Monday issued a rule that explains how it would enforce a program for cleaner cars nationwide if the automakers and states can reach a deal on the program.

"It's a procedural step that establishes the enforcement framework that will be necessary to bring the cleaner car off the drawing board into the show room, if in fact a deal is struck between the car manufacturers and the states," an EPA official said.

The automakers and northeastern states that are members of a regional organization to deal with air quality issues are negotiating offering a less-polluting car in all states except California, which has even stricter air quality requirements. The program is voluntary, but needs some rules from the EPA.

The carmakers proposed a national program for a cleaner gasoline-powered vehicles as an alternative to the northeast states demand that even cleaner cars, including some electric and natural gas vehicles, be sold in their region. The talks were stalled by a dispute over Massachusetts and New York's requirements that electric cars be offered in those states. But last month the carmakers agreed to handle that dispute through lawsuits and separate it from the clean-car talks.
